step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Two concurrent adult male patients in Northern Central African Republic (Case 1: 28-year-old male squirrel hunter; Case 2: 26-year-old male farmer); primary patient anchor is Case 1 (patient_1).

step4_condition_matched: Filovirus infection (tested in regional reference laboratory in Bangui alongside Dengue and Yellow Fever)

evidence_items.source_quote: Filovirus and Dengue infections were tested for and revealed negative results.
Filo-, Yellow Fever and Dengue virus infections were ruled out.

step10_contradiction_notes: No positive filovirus claim exists; reference laboratory testing in Bangui explicitly ruled out filovirus infection in both patients.
rationale: A 28-year-old male hunter in the Central African Republic (alongside a 26-year-old farmer) presented with fever, myalgia, bullous/vesicular skin lesions, shock, epistaxis, and hematemesis. Because of hemorrhagic manifestations, blood and vesicular fluid samples were sent to the regional reference laboratory in Bangui, where Filovirus and Dengue infections were explicitly tested for and returned negative results ('Filovirus and Dengue infections were tested for and revealed negative results'; 'Filo-, Yellow Fever and Dengue virus infections were ruled out'). Target disease concept is grounded, assertion is NEGATED, clinical role is RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, and evidence is E0_CONTRADICTED -> NEGATIVE.
